message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    We prove an algebraicity criterion for leaves of algebraic foliations defined over number fields. Namely, consider a number field
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>K</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    embedded in
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>C</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    , a smooth algebraic variety
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>X</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    over
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>K</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    , equipped with a
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mrow>
                        <mml:mi>K</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>-</mml:mo>
                      </mml:mrow>
                    </mml:math>
                    rational point
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>P</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    , and
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>F</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    an algebraic subbundle of the its tangent bundle
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:msub>
                        <mml:mi>T</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>X</mml:mi>
                      </mml:msub>
                    </mml:math>
                    , defined over
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>K</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    . Assume moreover that the vector bundle
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>F</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    is involutive, i.e., closed under Lie bracket. Then it defines an holomorphic foliation of the analytic manifold
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mrow>
                        <mml:mi>X</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mi>C</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                      </mml:mrow>
                    </mml:math>
                    , and one may consider its leaf
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>F</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    through
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>P</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    . We prove that F is algebraic if the following local conditions are satisfied:
i) For almost every prime ideal
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>p</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    of the ring of integers
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mrow>
                        <mml:mi>𝒪</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>K</mml:mi>
                      </mml:mrow>
                    </mml:math>
                    of the number field K, the
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>p</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    -curvature of the reduction modulo
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>p</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    of the involutive bundle F vanishes at P (where p denotes the characteristic of the residue field O K/p). ii) The analytic manifold F satisfies the Liouville property; this arises, in particular, if F is the image by some holomorphic map of the complement in a complex algebraic variety of a closed analytic subset. This algebraicity criterion unifies and extends various results of D. V. and G. V. Chudnovsky, André, and Graftieaux, and also admits new consequences. For instance, applied to an algebraic group G over K, it shows that a K-Lie subalgebra h of Lie G is algebraic if and only if for almost every non-zero prime ideal p of O K, of residue characteristic p, the reduction modulo p of h is a restricted Lie subalgebra of the reduction modulo p of Lie G (i.e., is stable under p-th powers). This solves a conjecture of Ekedahl and Shepherd-Barron. The algebraicity criterion above follows from a more basic algebraicity criterion concerning smooth formal germs in algebraic varieties over number fields. The proof of the latter relies on “transcendence techniques”, recast in a modern geometric version involving elementary concepts of Arakelov geometry, and on some analytic estimates, related to the First Main Theorem of higher-dimensional Nevanlinna theory.
                  </jats:p>
